The '''1684 Ayuman Cup''', recognised retrospectively as the 7th edition of the '''[[FLLA World Cup]]''', was an international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the leading Ayuman football associations. It was held in [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]], across [[Ayuma]], from 5 June to 4 July 1684, and was won by the hosts, [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]], who defeated [[Siana]] 4–2 in the [[#Final|final]] at the Shurqan Grand Stadium to claim their first title.<ref name="heritage-overview">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1684/overview|title=The 1684 Ayuman Cup: tournament overview|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=11 June 1763}}</ref>

The tournament was the last edition contested before the [[Red War]] (1688 to 1695), which forced the cancellation of the three scheduled editions of [[1688 FLLA World Cup|1688]], [[1692 FLLA World Cup|1692]] and [[1696 FLLA World Cup|1696]] and the longest hiatus in the competition's history. It was staged under the older title of the Ayuman Cup, the name the competition bore before the [[FLLA]] was constituted and the contest was relaunched and renamed the [[FLLA World Cup]] at the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]]; the seven continental confederations did not yet exist, and the field was drawn mainly from [[Ayuma]], though it now included associations from beyond the continent, among them [[Raledria]] of [[Atirha]] and [[Taval]] and [[Trian]] of [[Mahea]].<ref name="heritage-rename">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/history/early-competition-names|title=From the Ayuman Cup to the FLLA World Cup: the early names of the competition|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=12 February 1764}}</ref>

The 1684 edition was contested for the original rotating '''[[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]]''', which was presented to the victorious Alzurian side at the close of the final. It proved to be the last occasion on which the original trophy was awarded: the cup remained in [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]] after the victory and was destroyed there at the outbreak of the [[Red War]] in 1688, before a replacement could be contested for. No bespoke permanent trophy was commissioned in 1684; the permanent-trophy tradition that came to characterise the competition began only with the Solana at the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]], after the loss of the original cup.<ref name="heritage-trophy">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/trophies/the-andah-cup|title=The original Andah Cup and its loss in 1688|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=2 July 1764}}</ref>

==Host selection==

The 1684 tournament was awarded to [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]] by a congress of the Ayuman national associations, the informal body that organised the competition before the foundation of the [[FLLA]]. The hosting was regarded at the time as a measure of recompense to the Alzurian Union, which had been awarded the cancelled [[1664 FLLA World Cup|1664 edition]] before the outbreak of the [[Great Imperial War]] forced its abandonment. The Alzurian organisers undertook to stage the finals across six cities of the union, with the principal matches held in the capital, [[Shurqan]].<ref name="heritage-host">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1684/host|title=1684 Ayuman Cup: the award of hosting rights to Alzuria|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=11 June 1763}}</ref>

==Format==

The 16 entered teams were divided into four groups of four for the group stage. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing the other three sides in its group; two points were awarded for a win and one for a draw, in line with the scoring system then in use. The top two teams in each group advanced to the [[#Knockout stage|knockout stage]], while the bottom two were eliminated. Where teams finished level on points, places were determined first by goal difference and then by goals scored.

The knockout stage consisted of single-elimination ties played over 90 minutes. A tie level at the end of normal time was extended by a single 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]]; under the regulations of the period, any tie still level after extra time was to be settled by a replay rather than by a [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]], a procedure not yet in use. No replay proved necessary in 1684. The two losing semi-finalists contested a [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] on the day before the final.

==Participating teams==

Sixteen teams took part in the 1684 finals, most of them Ayuman national associations. The continental confederations that later structured the [[FLLA World Cup]] had not yet been established, and qualification was settled under the informal arrangements of the period; as host nation, [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]] took part automatically. The field also included associations from beyond [[Ayuma]]: [[Raledria]], an [[Atirha]]n side that would go on to host and win the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|first edition under the World Cup name]], and the [[Mahea]]n associations of [[Taval]] and [[Trian]]. The participating teams were:<ref name="heritage-teams">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1684/teams|title=1684 Ayuman Cup: participating teams|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 June 1763}}</ref>

==Venues==

Six stadiums in six host cities, all in [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]], were used in the final tournament. The principal venue was the Shurqan Grand Stadium in the capital, [[Shurqan]], which staged the opening match and the final and was the only ground with a capacity above 30,000. The two semi-finals were divided between the Turashik Arena in [[Turashik]] and the Veshgadar Stadium in [[Veshgadar]], with the [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] held at Borshavi Park in [[Borshavi]]. The remaining group-stage fixtures were shared between these grounds and the two smallest venues, at [[Zarhesh]] and [[Havrishka]].<ref name="heritage-venues">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1684/venues|title=Host stadiums of the 1684 Ayuman Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 June 1763}}</ref>

==Squads==

Each participating association registered a squad of eighteen players, two of whom were required to be goalkeepers; the smaller squads of the period reflected the limited substitution rules then in force, under which a single replacement was permitted only for an injured goalkeeper. A total of 288 players were registered for the tournament.<ref name="heritage-squads">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1684/squads|title=1684 Ayuman Cup: registered squads|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 June 1763}}</ref>

==Match officials==

The organising congress appointed a panel of referees and linesmen drawn from the associations not represented in the latter stages of the competition. The opening match was refereed by Joren Aldal of [[Verusa]], and the final by Mikol Trenz of [[Eldjo]], the senior official of the tournament. The small officiating pool of the period meant that several referees took charge of fixtures involving teams from neighbouring associations, though never from their own.<ref name="heritage-officials">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1684/officials|title=Match officials of the 1684 Ayuman Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 June 1763}}</ref>

==Group stage==

The four groups were each contested as a single round-robin. The top two teams in each group advanced to the knockout stage; points were awarded on the two-points-for-a-win system in use at the time, with goal difference and then goals scored used to separate teams level on points.

All dates are given in the local time of the host cities.

==Knockout stage==

The knockout stage involved the eight teams that advanced from the group stage, with each group winner drawn against a runner-up from another group. Ties level after 90 minutes were extended by a single period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]]; one of the four quarter-finals was decided in the additional period. No tie required a replay.

===Final===

The final was held at the Shurqan Grand Stadium on 4 July 1684 before an estimated crowd of 30,000. [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]] took the lead early through Konrad Veitz, the tournament's leading scorer, and led 2–0 through Heinric Marold before [[Siana]] drew level with goals from Aldo Feronti and Renso Mazzo. Marold restored the lead with his second, and Anders Halden added a fourth late on, for a 4–2 finish. The victory secured Alzuria's first title, won on home soil, and the original [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]] was presented to the Alzurian captain at the close of the match.<ref name="heritage-final">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1684/final|title=The 1684 Ayuman Cup final: Alzuria 4–2 Siana|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=11 June 1763}}</ref>

==Statistics==

===Goalscorers===

A total of 83 goals were scored in 32 matches, an average of 2.59 per match. The leading scorer was the Alzurian forward Konrad Veitz, who scored seven goals across the tournament, including one in the final. No formal individual awards were presented at the 1684 edition: the leading-player, top-scorer and best-goalkeeper prizes (the [[FLLA World Cup#Awards|Vairan Ball, Marskval and Bastion]]) were not instituted until the [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744 edition]], and the figures below are recognised retrospectively in the [[FLLA]]'s heritage records.<ref name="heritage-stats">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1684/statistics|title=1684 Ayuman Cup statistical record|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 June 1763}}</ref>

==Trophy and significance==

The 1684 edition holds a distinctive place in the history of the [[FLLA World Cup]] as the last tournament contested before the [[Red War]] and the last for which the original rotating [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]] was awarded. Alzuria's victory on home soil was the high point of Alzurian football of the period, and the only major title the union would win.<ref name="heritage-overview" />

The cup that Alzuria lifted was the same trophy that had been contested since its introduction at the [[1668 FLLA World Cup|1668 edition]]. Following the Alzurian win it remained in the union, and was destroyed there at the outbreak of the [[Red War]] in 1688, with the [[1688 FLLA World Cup|1688 edition]] that had been awarded to [[Raledria]] abandoned before it could be played. When the competition was relaunched and renamed the [[FLLA World Cup]] at the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]], no rotating cup was available, and the host association instead commissioned a bespoke permanent trophy, beginning the permanent-trophy tradition that has characterised the competition ever since.<ref name="heritage-trophy" />

The three editions of [[1688 FLLA World Cup|1688]], [[1692 FLLA World Cup|1692]] and [[1696 FLLA World Cup|1696]] were all cancelled because of the war and the subsequent reconstruction, making 1684 the last edition of the competition for sixteen years.<ref name="heritage-rename" />
